newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Volatility stymies strategists.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Volatility stymies strategists.

text.p: Options traders and strategists often use spikes in volatility to make money, but this week's increase has provided few opportunities because of the speed with which the market has whipsawed between plus and minus.
"I don't know anybody who can put a prudent strategy together in the face of this," said Jerry Hegarty, an analyst at Thomson Financial.
"Something major appears to be changing, but on the other hand, ever since the (1987) crash, whenever there's been a pullback, the bulls have been able to recover and make new highs," he said.
"It's very hard to bet against that, as ugly as it looks right now," Hegarty said.

By 1200 CST/1800 GMT, the key Dow industrial average was up about five points at 6,309. The index fell sharply in early trading, triggering New York Stock Exchange trading curbs which were in effect for less than 10 minutes.
The blue chip index later rallied about 40 points before slipping back.
The S&P 100 index .OEX was down 0.61 at 705.82, having traded between 699.87 and 709.78. The S&P 500 index .SPX fell 1.70 to 727.63 after bouncing between 721.88 and 731.26.
"It's anything but a clear-cut situation," Hegarty said.
Robert Rack at Investment Research Institute said the spike in the CBOE's volatility index .VIX, which was up 1.49 at 23.28, would normally suggest a rally is in the offing.
But this time around, out-of-the-money index call volatilities have risen right along with out-of-the-money index put volatilities, indicating any bounce will be small.
"It's encouraging that the VIX is spiking, but I don't think call implied volatilities have died to the point where we're going to see a strong bounce like we have in the past," Rack said.
He said the call implied volatilities were around 17 but need to be in the low teens "to make me feel like we've hit a bottom".
Put volatilities were in the low 20's.
Hegarty said his "best guess" was that the market would be able to work its way higher over the very near term but that the trading pattern so far in December makes him wary.
"On three of the nine trading days, the (SPX) futures have gone out within 0.50 of their (intraday) lows," he explained. "That's dangerous because bull markets should be strong late in the day."
"There are definitely warning signals out there," he said. "At some point you ought to step back and say, I need to see more" before making a move.

Friday's volatility appeared to keep investors focused on index puts, particularly in the OEX, where the December 700 put traded 22,475 contracts, the December 705 put more than 17,800 and the December 710 put around 13,125.
The most active call was the December 720, with nearly 13,000 contracts changing hands. The December 710 call traded 11,200. ((G. Crawford, 312 408 8750/Email: derivatives@reuters.com))
